summary: This Wikipedia article profiles James Cleverly, a British Conservative politician and Army Reserve officer who has been Home Secretary since November 2023 and MP for Braintree since 2015. It traces his education, military service, and London Assembly career, then his parliamentary and ministerial roles, including Foreign Secretary from 2022 to 2023 and Education Secretary in July 2022. The note is cut off partway through the July 2022 section of his political career.
one_line: James Cleverly is a British Conservative MP, Army Reserve officer, and Home Secretary since November 2023, formerly Foreign Secretary.
key_facts: James Spencer Cleverly was born on 4 September 1969 in Lewisham, London, England.
Cleverly has served as Home Secretary of the United Kingdom since 13 November 2023.
Cleverly was Foreign Secretary from 6 September 2022 to 13 November 2023, appointed by Prime Minister Liz Truss.
Cleverly was the first British foreign secretary of African heritage, according to the note.
Cleverly has been the Member of Parliament for Braintree in Essex since 7 May 2015.
In the 2015 general election Cleverly won 53.8% of the vote in Braintree with a majority of 17,610.
Cleverly was a Member of the London Assembly for Bexley and Bromley from 4 May 2008 to 5 May 2016.
Cleverly was appointed Secretary of State for Education from 7 July 2022 to 6 September 2022.
Cleverly was promoted to lieutenant colonel on 1 March 2015 and serves in the Army Reserve with the Royal Artillery.
Cleverly was educated at Riverston School and Colfe's School in Lee, London, and graduated with a Bachelor of Arts from Ealing College of Higher Education in 1991.
Cleverly was commissioned into the Army Reserve as a second lieutenant (acting) on 6 October 1991.
In 2016 Cleverly was asked to step down as patron of Advocacy for All after voting to cut Employment and Support Allowance.
Cleverly announced on 29 May 2019 that he was standing in the 2019 Conservative leadership election and withdrew on 4 June 2019.
As Home Secretary, Cleverly has committed to maintaining the Rwanda asylum plan and plans to substantially reduce legal migration by raising the threshold for family visas.
